yaa-asantewaa.s: Yaa Asantewaa was the Queen Mother of Ejisu in the Ashanti Empire, who led the War of the Golden Stool against British rule in 1900. The uprising was provoked by the British governor's demand to sit on the Golden Stool.

yahya-ibn-ibrahim.s: Yahya ibn Ibrahim was a chief of the Gudala, a Sanhaja Berber group of the western Sahara, in the eleventh century. Returning from pilgrimage to Mecca around 1040, he met the jurist Abu Imran al-Fasi in Kairouan, a contact that led to the scholar Abd Allah ibn Yasin being sent…

yam-postal-system.s: The Yam was the relay and postal system of the Mongol Empire, a network of stations supplying fresh horses, food and lodging to official messengers and travellers. It allowed information and orders to travel rapidly across the vast empire.

yamama.s: Yamama is a historical region of central Arabia, in the area of present-day Riyadh. After the death of the Prophet Muhammad it was the base of the rival prophet Musaylima.

yangtze-river.s: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in Asia, flowing from the Tibetan plateau east to the sea at Shanghai. Its basin became China's economic heartland, producing rice, silk, tea and other goods.

yaqub-al-mansur.s: Yaqub al-Mansur was the third Almohad caliph, reigning from 1184 to 1199. He won a great victory over Castile at the Battle of Alarcos in 1195, earning the title al-Mansur, 'made victorious by God', and raided as far as the walls of Toledo.

yaqub-ibn-killis.s: Ya'qub ibn Killis was a statesman of the Fatimid Caliphate, a convert from Judaism who became the first Fatimid vizier in Egypt in the tenth century. He organised the financial and administrative system of the new Fatimid state.

yarkent-khanate.s: The Yarkent Khanate was a successor state of the eastern Chagatai realm, centred on the oasis city of Yarkand in the western Tarim Basin. The Chagatai Empire profile notes that the eastern khanate split around 1462 into the Yarkent and Turpan khanates.

yasa.s: The Yasa was the body of law and decrees attributed to Genghis Khan, governing military discipline, administration and social conduct among the Mongols. It served as a foundation of Mongol imperial governance.

yazdegerd-iii.s: Yazdegerd III was the last king of the Sasanian Empire, who came to the throne as a youth in the 630s. His reign saw the Arab conquest of Iran, with decisive defeats at al-Qadisiyya and Nahavand.

yazid-i.s: Yazid I was the second Umayyad caliph, reigning from 680 to 683, the son of Muawiya. His succession was contested, and his reign saw the killing of Husayn ibn Ali at Karbala in 680 and the revolt of Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.

year-name.s: A year-name was a dating formula used in early Mesopotamia, in which each year was named after a notable event of the previous year, such as a military victory or the building of a temple. The Babylonian Empire profile notes that Hammurabi's year-names, attached by scribes to…

yejju-dynasty.s: The Yejju dynasty was an Oromo family of regional lords from Yejju in north-central Ethiopia who dominated the Ethiopian court during the Zemene Mesafint. The Ethiopian Empire profile notes that, while many emperors occupied the throne, real governance passed to Ras regents of…

yekuno-amlak.s: Yekuno Amlak was an emperor of Ethiopia who seized power from the Zagwe dynasty in 1270. He founded the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba and ruled Ethiopia, with interruptions, until 1974.

yellow-river.s: The Yellow River is the second-longest river in China, flowing from the Tibetan plateau across the north China plain to the Bohai Sea. It is considered the cradle of Chinese civilisation but is notorious for devastating floods and changes of course.

yellow-river-floods-of-1344.s: The Yellow River floods of 1344 were catastrophic floods in which the river burst its dykes and shifted its course, devastating agriculture across the north China plain. The Yuan Dynasty profile records that the floods destroyed agricultural production and displaced millions…

yellow-turban-rebellion.s: The Yellow Turban Rebellion was a large peasant uprising in China that began in 184 CE, led by the Taoist faith healer Zhang Jue and his brothers. Driven by millenarian expectations and agrarian distress, it spread across much of northern China.

yemen.s: Yemen is a region in the south-west of the Arabian Peninsula, historically a centre of trade in incense and a link between Arabia, the Horn of Africa and the Indian Ocean. The Aksumite Empire extended its control over Yemen in the sixth century before being expelled by the…

yenisei-kyrgyz.s: The Yenisei Kyrgyz were a Turkic people of the upper Yenisei River region in southern Siberia. The Gokturk Empire profile records that Qapaghan Qaghan conquered the Yenisei Kyrgyz and killed their qaghan in personal combat in 710.

yermak-timofeyevich.s: Yermak Timofeyevich was a Cossack leader who led an expedition across the Ural Mountains into Siberia in the 1580s, defeating the Khanate of Sibir. His campaigns from 1581 onward opened the way for Russian expansion across northern Asia.

yhwh.s: YHWH, conventionally rendered as Yahweh, is the name of the God of Israel in the Hebrew Bible. The Assyrian Empire profile notes that the Assyrian deportation of the population of the Kingdom of Israel had consequences for Jewish religious thought.

yiddish.s: Yiddish is a language of the Ashkenazi Jews, based on medieval German with Hebrew, Aramaic and Slavic elements and written in the Hebrew alphabet. It became the everyday language of Jewish communities across central and eastern Europe.

yijing.s: Yijing was a Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled by sea to India in the late seventh century, staying in Srivijaya on his journeys and visiting it in 671 CE. He studied Sanskrit there and described the kingdom as a major centre of Buddhist learning.

yin-shan.s: The Yin Shan are a range of mountains in Inner Mongolia, north of the great bend of the Yellow River. They formed a frontier zone between the Chinese plains and the steppe.

yongle-emperor.s: The Yongle Emperor was the third emperor of the Ming Empire, reigning from 1402 to 1424 after seizing the throne from his nephew. He moved the capital to Beijing, began construction of the Forbidden City and campaigned against the Mongols.

yongzheng-emperor.s: The Yongzheng Emperor was the third Qing emperor to rule China, reigning from 1722 to 1735 between the Kangxi and Qianlong emperors. He strengthened central administration, created the Grand Council and reformed taxation, curbing corruption among officials.

yoruba.s: The Yoruba are a major West African people of south-western Nigeria and neighbouring Benin, with a long tradition of urban city-states and the sacred city of Ile-Ife. The Oyo Empire was the most powerful Yoruba state, dominating the region from the seventeenth to the early…

yuan-dynasty.s: The Yuan Dynasty was the Mongol-ruled dynasty of China, proclaimed by Kublai Khan in 1271, which completed the conquest of the Southern Song in 1279. It made Beijing, then Dadu, its capital, promoted trade across Eurasia and patronised Tibetan Buddhism.

yuezhi.s: The Yuezhi were a nomadic people who lived in the region of the Gansu corridor in north-western China in the late first millennium BCE. Defeated by the Xiongnu in the second century BCE, they migrated westwards to Central Asia, where one branch later founded the Kushan Empire.

yugoslavia.s: Yugoslavia was a state of the South Slavs in the Balkans, proclaimed in 1918 as the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes from territories including former Austro-Hungarian lands. The Austro-Hungarian Empire profile lists it among the successor states of the empire.

yunfa.s: Yunfa was a sultan of the Hausa kingdom of Gobir and a former pupil of Usman dan Fodio. His conflict with dan Fodio's community triggered the jihad of 1804 that founded the Sokoto Caliphate.

yusuf-ibn-tashfin.s: Yusuf ibn Tashfin was the leader of the Almoravid Empire who died in 1106. He founded Marrakesh as the Almoravid capital, completed the conquest of Morocco and, at the invitation of the taifa kings, intervened in Iberia, defeating Alfonso VI of Castile at Sagrajas in 1086.

yusuf-ii.s: Yusuf II was an Almohad caliph who reigned from 1214 to 1224, succeeding his father Muhammad al-Nasir after the catastrophic defeat at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212. He came to the throne young and ruled weakly.
